title: 2 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 6
description: Ten questions on 2 Corinthians 6: now is the day of salvation, the long list of what the servants of God endure, and the call to be separate.

questions.text: What does the writer entreat them not to do with the grace of God?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says: Working together, we entreat also that you do not receive the grace of God in vain.

answers.text: Not to receive the grace of God in vain
Not to speak of the grace of God to outsiders
Not to measure the grace of God by themselves
Not to boast in the grace of God

questions.text: What does verse 2 say about the present moment?
questions.explanation: After quoting, "At an acceptable time I listened to you. In a day of salvation I helped you", verse 2 says: Behold, now is the acceptable time. Behold, now is the day of salvation.

answers.text: That the day of salvation is still far off
That the acceptable time has already passed
That now is the acceptable time and now is the day of salvation
That no one knows the acceptable time

questions.text: Why do they give no occasion of stumbling in anything?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says they give no occasion of stumbling in anything, so that their service may not be blamed.

answers.text: So that they may be praised by all men
So that their service may not be blamed
So that they may receive a gift
So that they may be sent to Macedonia

questions.text: Which of these does the text list among the things in which they commend themselves as servants of God?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 lists beatings, imprisonments, riots, labors, watchings, and fastings.

answers.text: Feasts, festivals and new moons
Visions, dreams and revelations
Signs, wonders and mighty works
Beatings, imprisonments and riots

questions.text: What pairs does verse 8 set side by side?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says: by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true.

answers.text: Glory and dishonor, evil report and good report, deceivers and yet true
Rich and poor, strong and weak, wise and foolish
Light and darkness, righteousness and iniquity
Flesh and spirit, letter and Spirit

questions.text: How does verse 10 describe them in regard to riches and possessions?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.

answers.text: As rich, yet making many poor; as having all things
As poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things
As having all things, and yet needing everything from them
As wealthy, and yet sharing nothing at all with anyone

questions.text: What does the writer say about his mouth and his heart toward the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says: Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians. Our heart is enlarged.

answers.text: His mouth is closed and his heart is heavy
His mouth speaks in parables and his heart is hidden
His mouth is open to them and his heart is enlarged
His mouth is silent until he comes

questions.text: What warning does verse 14 give about unbelievers?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says: Don't be unequally yoked with unbelievers, for what fellowship do righteousness and iniquity have? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?

answers.text: To judge them before the assembly
To take nothing from them
To teach them the law first
Not to be unequally yoked with them

questions.text: What does verse 16 say the Corinthians are?
questions.explanation: Verse 16 asks what agreement a temple of God has with idols, and says: For you are a temple of the living God.

answers.text: A temple of the living God
A letter sealed with the Spirit
An assembly of Macedonia
A house not made with hands

questions.text: What does the Lord promise in the words quoted in verses 17 and 18?
questions.explanation: The quotation says: Come out from among them, and be separate, touch no unclean thing, I will receive you; I will be to you a Father, and you will be to me sons and daughters.

answers.text: That he will give them the land of Achaia for their possession
That he will receive them and be a Father to them, and they will be sons and daughters to him
That he will send them many adversaries in order to test them
That he will keep a veil on their hearts until the very end
